question.problem:
Let $D$ be the finite region bounded by the curve 
$y-{({y}^{2}+\frac{x}{2})}^{2}=-5$ and the line $y=4.$ Consider the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where $u={y}^{2}+\frac{x}{2}$ and $v=y.$ Find the representation of ${T}^{-1}(D)$ in the $uv$-plane.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we are given that 

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+\frac{x}{2} \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting ${y}^{2}+\frac{x}{2}=u$ and $y=v$ into the equation of the first curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{({y}^{2}+\frac{x}{2})}^{2}=-5\,⟹\,v-{u}^{2}=-5\,⟹\,v={u}^{2}-5,\end{aligned}
$$

while substituting $y=v$ into the equation of the second curve, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y=4\,⟹\,v=4.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the intersections of the curves in the $uv$-plane, we solve the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}v={u}^{2}-5 \\ v=4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}u=\pm 3 \\ v=4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection points are $(\pm 3,4).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14166956/assets/fe39efb538d3270028fa5892402d56a8ae0e061968ecca8c676d8ad9f482644e.png)

As a result, our domain in the $uv$-plane has the type I representation 

$$
{T}^{-1}(D)=\{(u,v)\,:\,-3\le u\le 3,\,{u}^{2}-5\le v\le 4\}.
$$
